articleSummary:
- Nigeria reports a single confirmed Ebola case with a genetic link to a Kenyan strain, marking the first genomic connection between outbreaks in Nigeria and Kenya. Nigeria says there is no evidence the Kenyan patient traveled to Nigeria or direct contact between patients; authorities are tracing contacts and quarantining them, with several contacts testing negative and others awaiting results. The Nigerian case involved a traveler who had visited Uganda, and Uganda remains Ebola-free but has tightened border controls and requires traveler-location forms for all arrivals, including a ban on entry for those who visited the Democratic Republic of Congo. Regional coordination among Nigeria, Kenya, and Uganda is emphasized, with laboratories ready to process samples and a commitment to transpare
- DR Congo has begun a vaccine trial to curb the Bundibugyo-ebola variant, the driver of the worst outbreak in the country’s history, with more than 4,600 deaths and about 9,700 infections since mid-May. There is currently no approved vaccine specific to Bundibugyo. articleHeadline: Model maps cheapest routes to end sleeping sickness transmission in DRC
articleSummary: Gambiense human African trypanosomiasis (gHAT) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is analyzed via cost-effectiveness modelling across 165 health zones for 2026–2040. Six strategies—ranging from status quo control to elimination-by-2030 or elimination-by-2040—are assessed within a net monetary framework using costs per disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) averted. By 2030, strategies prioritising elimination predict transmission reduction in 118–134 health zones; by 2040, costs would total $67.8M, $93.3M, and $185M (with wide prediction intervals). A looser 2040 target yields elimination in 152 zones at ~ $158M, leaving 13 zones unmet. In 2026, front-loaded spending differs markedly: status quo about $8.75M versus elimination strategies about $27.0M. Pursuing 2030 elimination could reduce gHAT deaths by 68% (7,979 deaths under status quo to 2,576). Some zones may still need novel tools to close gaps; results are interval-based, not precise forecasts.

articleHeadline: Cleaning tables, chairs, and toys to prevent hand, foot, and mouth disease.
articleSummary: HFMD is circulating year-round in Vietnam, with peaks in September–October, especially in kindergartens where children share toys and surfaces. It is caused by enteroviruses and spreads via saliva, respiratory secretions, vesicle fluid, and feces; contaminated toys and furniture enable transmission as children touch them and then put hands to the mouth. Incubation is 3–7 days; contagious 2–3 days before symptoms and throughout illness, with viral shedding in stool weeks after recovery in young children. Alcohol-based sanitizers are less effective against these viruses; chlorine-based disinfectants (active chlorine) such as Cloramin B or Javene are recommended at correct dilutions. Cocoliztli epidemics in 1545–1576 in Mexico caused ~15 million deaths, linked to Salmonella enterica Paratyphi C by ancient DNA. The Third Pandemic of plague (1855) killed 12–15 million; the Antonine Plague (165–180) likely smallpox, 5–10 million. The 1957–1958 Asian Flu (H2N2) caused about 1–4 million.
